blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Prehistory refers to the era before the invention of writing, relying solely on non-literary evidence.
Archaeological evidence includes stone tools, bones, fossils, cave paintings, and habitation sites.
The Prehistoric Age is classified based on the nature and refinement of tools used by early humans.
Tool refinement directly reflects changes in human lifestyle and social organisation.

blocks.content: Prehistory refers to the long span of human past before the invention of writing. Since writing had not yet developed, historians cannot rely on inscriptions, manuscripts, or literary sources to understand this period. Instead, the reconstruction of prehistoric life depends entirely on archaeological evidence such as stone tools, bones, fossils, cave paintings, and habitation sites.
Prehistory refers to the long span of human past before the invention of writing.
In competitive examinations like SSC, a very clear distinction is made: - History deals with written records. - Prehistory deals with periods where no written records exist.

blocks.content: This distinction is extremely important for objective-type questions.
Basis of Classification of the Prehistoric Age

The Prehistoric Age is classified mainly on the basis of the tools used by humans. As humans progressed, their tools became more refined, which also reflects changes in their lifestyle and social organisation.

items: Distinction tested in SSC: History deals with written records, whereas Prehistory deals with periods without written records.
Questions frequently ask about the primary basis of classification of Prehistory (Answer: Tools used by humans).
Memorize the sequence line for SSC questions: Pa – Me – Neo – Chal.
